summary.text: Pamela Michos is the Republican and Conservative Party candidate for New York State Senate District 11, running against incumbent Toby Ann Stavisky.
A Whitestone native, she describes a career in banking, financial services and wealth management, and she is PTA president of a Greek school in Flushing.
This is her first run for public office.

paragraphs.text: Michos is a Whitestone, Queens native of Greek (Kefalonian) descent, according to a National Herald report, and an endorsing club describes her as a single mother and Greek Orthodox Christian.

According to her campaign website, she graduated from New York University's Steinhardt School, where she studied Nutrition and Food Studies with a concentration in Clinical Dietetics, and earned an Associate degree in Liberal Arts from Nassau Community College, graduating magna cum laude.
The website also says she developed health literacy programs for underserved communities in the Bronx and was recognized by NYC Health + Hospitals for her service.

Her campaign website says Michos has nearly a decade of experience in banking, financial services and wealth management and nearly 14 years of executive leadership experience with publicly traded companies, and that she is a former small business owner.
An endorsing club describes her as having "managed billions of dollars."
She serves as PTA president of the Stefanos and Areti Cherpelis Hellenic School of Saint Nicholas Greek Orthodox Church in Flushing.
She is running on the Republican and Conservative Party lines, and a campaign fundraiser was held in Bayside in September under the slogan "Protect the American Dream."
